15 Types of People You Find in Every Gym - How many do you recognise?

I'm like a mixture of the couch potato and the dude. I have to take a lot of breaks between sets due to a medical condition so I tend to spend a lot of time doing nothing while I let myself cool off. I'm very, very cautious about my form due to past experiences and injuries.

I'm no expert but I can tell you the best kind of routine I've seen to work for newbs.

I'd recommend that gaining strength and doing the exercises that give you the best full body workout are the ones that every newbie should focus on. Light free weight exercise with very slow controlled form preferably with someone with you to watch your form is the best route to start. You want to have clean form on deadlifts, squats, push-ups, benchpress (incline too) , dumbbell lunges, close and wide grip pullups (you may need to use machines at first depending on your body weight or an assistance machine), Bent-over rows, dumbbell rows, dumbbell fly's (incline too). Do 5x5 sets in each exercise with a weight that is a little more(10-25% more) than you could do a single set of 10 reps with. Ex) If you could do 10 reps squating 150 then do 5 reps at 165 or up to 190ish, where ever inbetween you feel good about. You'll learn a great deal about your body this way and figure out where you are stronger or weaker. Size and body shape play a lot into what you'll be able to do. This kind of work out will build strength and muscle mass very steadily in my experience.

Stretching after every workout is essential. Before is good too, but there's a bit of a debate about that when it comes to strength training that I don't want to go into. Do lots of stretches for your legs and your groin and your lower back, especially if you've had back problems in the past.

If you're trying to lose weight the best way is to stop thinking in terms of weight and think in terms of fat. You want to lose that fat. Building strength builds muscles and bigger muscles use more energy (calories) so you'll naturally start losing fat as you gain muscle and you'll look better. If you want to lose fat faster then, before your stretching, after your lift do some cardio (treadmill, elliptical, row-machine, bike, walk a mile or two) and you'll be using those primed muscles in a way that is much better than just going for a jog so you'll be burning more calories.

Also I'd recommend recording your progress in an app like myfitnesspal . Great for figuring out your diet and maintaining your goals.

Lastly and most importantly, rest. 3 to 4 days a week at the gym is perfect in my opinion. Don't feel like you need to be there everyday, you don't. Drink a shit-ton of water and get 8 hours of sleep a night everynight. You'll progress very fast this way.

Also... if you don't have a gym partner then don't worry because there will definitely be someone at the gym who is willing to spot you on exercises.
